I've got some problems with this article. They're basically comparing rats to humans and saying "if the rat eats X amount of HFCS it gets obese, it follows that humans will also get obese". The article completely glosses over the fact that the rat is not only a fraction of the mass of a human (average healthy rat is about 360g, while a human is well over 100x that) and also has a much faster metabolic rate. A healthy rat heartbeat is 330-480 bpm, while a human's is 100 bpm.

All they've really proven here is that X amount is not good for rats. No effort was made to figure out what acceptable levels are. Further, they make a point of saying that HFCS causes the body to store fat in a specific place (belly fat), but that it's not inherently more fat than the same amount of calories from a differing food. The article makes a distinction, but makes no real effort to describe why this is bad.

Then there's the heading the OP chose to post under:

"How Added Sugar Consumption makes you fat, lazy, less intelligent, depressed, and mentally and physically unhealthy"

The article doesn't talk about levels of activity, intelligence, mental state, or any potential physical problems other than weight gain which is not adequately quantified.
